collection_title: Syndrome and medication index of the ICMR Treatment Guidelines for Antimicrobial Use in Common Syndromes, 2022-23 edition
provenance_note: Conditions in this file are attributed to the ICMR Treatment Guidelines 2022-23 edition on the basis of operator attestation. The seven files in transcription_sources are Google Docs exports carrying no issuing organization, author or date of their own; they are hashed and recorded as transcriptions, never as independent authorities. Because no official 2022-23 PDF is held, NO record in this file carries a page number in the authority document. Where the same text also occurs in the hash-verified 2019 edition, that location is recorded separately as a prior-edition cross-reference and must not be presented as a 2022-23 page.
transcription_note: Measured against the ingested 2019 corpus, 80 of 82 extracts are verbatim identical and the remaining two exceed 70% four-gram overlap. Such continuity is expected between editions of the same guideline. A residue of content -- ceftazidime-avibactam for HAP/VAP among it -- is absent from the 2019 edition entirely and is flagged as new or revised in this edition.

iai_community_mild_moderate.verbatim_extract: Community acquired intra-abdominal infection of mild to moderate severity
presentation: Infection spreading from the viscus into the peritoneum causing localized or diffuse peritonitis
Community onset
Mild to moderate severity

medications.note: If ESBL prevalence is under ten percent a third generation cephalosporin may be used, in which case metronidazole must be added.

spontaneous_bacterial_peritonitis_stg.verbatim_extract: Spontaneous bacterial peritonitis (SBP) refers to ascitic fluid infection with no recognizable source
presentation: Ascitic fluid infection with no recognizable source, commonly in cirrhosis
Ascitic fluid absolute polymorphonuclear leukocyte (PMN) count > 250 cells/mm3

spontaneous_bacterial_peritonitis_stg.comments: Antibiotics should be tailored as per the culture and sensitivity data. Ascitic fluid (at least 10 ml) should be inoculated into a blood culture bottle at the bedside. Up to 50% of patients with SBP have concomitant bacteraemia.

presentation: Acute onset of fever AND a change in mental status (confusion, disorientation, coma, or inability to talk)

acute_febrile_encephalopathy.comments: Acute febrile encephalopathy is a medical emergency. Empiric therapy should be started immediately after drawing blood cultures pending results of tests, then narrowed based on the results of investigations. Non infectious causes include Reye's syndrome, ADEM, metabolic/toxic encephalopathy, NCSE and autoimmune encephalitis.

acute_bacterial_meningitis.verbatim_extract: The administration of dexamethasone 15- 20 minutes prior to giving the first dose
presentation: Fever, altered sensorium, meningeal signs
CSF sent for cell count, sugar and protein, gram stain and culture
organisms: MRSA and Candida in late onset neonatal meningitis

adjunct_steroid: Dexamethasone 0.15 mg/kg every 6 hours for 48-96 hours (10 mg 6 hourly in adults), given 15-20 minutes prior to the first dose of antibiotic
escalation: Consider adding rifampicin if cephalosporin MIC >= 4 microgram/mL, if the condition worsens after 48 hours of vancomycin + ceftriaxone, if dexamethasone has been given, or if repeat LP shows the presence of bacteria

acute_bacterial_meningitis.duration: Generally 10-14 days for uncomplicated meningitis. Pathogen dependent: 7 days for meningococcus and H. influenzae, 10-14 days for pneumococcus, 2-3 weeks for group B Streptococcus, 3-6 weeks for Listeria, 3 weeks for gram negative meningitis.
acute_bacterial_meningitis.comments: Steroids are not recommended for meningitis in neonates. If the organism is cephalosporin susceptible, vancomycin can be stopped. In patients improving clinically there is no need to repeat CSF analysis.
